Original title: AI Filmmaking Tutorial: Scene Foundation for Consistent Multi-Angle Shots
Published: 2026-09-24T18:03:10+00:00

Video description only; transcript and video have not been retrieved.
Channel/community: peytonb37

Tired of AI shots that don’t match from angle to angle? In this video, I show my Scene Foundation method for AI filmmaking: build the world first (exterior + interior masters), then add characters, new angles, and lighting that stay consistent across a full sequence.
What you’ll learn:
- How to create a single-location horror house with consistent exteriors and interiors
- Seeding and inpainting tips to fix doors/windows and geometry mismatches
- Generating new angles and time-of-day variants (day, golden hour, midnight)
- Compositing characters with correct perspective, shadows, and mood
- Organizing boards and assembling a coherent edit
Tools mentioned:
- Higsfield image models (Nano, Cream) for photoreal coverage
- Adobe Firefly Boards for visual planning
- Vizard Agent for end-to-end, prompt-driven editing (fill missing shots, color grade, audio, export)
Why it works:
- Scene foundation anchors the model to real spatial data, reducing hallucinations and preserving continuity.
Workflow recap:
- Step 1: Generate exterior + interior masters from one foundational image
- Step 2: Expand angles; create day/night variants
- Step 3: Build a neutral-base character and outfits
- Step 4: Composite into rooms; refine with inpainting
- Step 5: Board it, then assemble a timeline or prompt Vizard Agent for an auto-cut
